question: I heard the Karnataka Rent Act caps the security deposit at 2 months' rent, so my landlord must refund the rest. Right?
answer: The Karnataka Rent Act does not set a specific limit of two months' rent for a security deposit. Section 17 deals with deposit of rent and other charges but does not mention any cap on the amount [KRA-s17-p2]. Section 15 provides that if any sum is paid in contravention of the Act, the Controller may order a refund to the tenant [KRA-s15].

question: My landlord deducted 25,000 from my 60,000 deposit for repainting the whole flat after I lived there 2 years.
answer: Under the Karnataka Rent Act a landlord may only deduct from the security deposit for damage that goes beyond normal wear and tear.  Section 47 says the premises must be kept in the same condition as when let, except for normal wear and tear, unless the written rent agreement says otherwise [KRA-s47-p1].  Repainting the whole flat after two years is usually considered normal wear, so the deduction is likely not allowed unless your lease specifically required you to repaint at the end of the tenancy.
